bottleneck:
The bottleneck is getting new long videos discovered. Shipping only broad topics didn't change that in week one, and production keeps losing the video most likely to help.

**New videos aren't being shown, whatever the topic.** The 6 long videos shipped from 11-17 to 11-22 were all broad, as last week's playbook asked. People click them: Nausea Foods 3.7% CTR, Mounjaro vs Zepbound 6.6%, Weight Loss 6.3%. But at days 1–5 each had only 64–124 impressions and 10–44 minutes. Last week's narrow videos had the same ceiling at that age. Diarrhea (narrow, 319 impressions, 22 search views) still beats every new broad video. So breadth alone hasn't lifted early discovery. The proven split (broad median about 490 lifetime minutes vs about 40 for narrow) mixes videos of different ages. Judge the new ones at day 14, not before.

**Watch time comes from a few old videos plus searched drug names.** The channel earns about 5–6 hours a day:
- EloraTZP has about 40% of lifetime minutes (5,255) and 11 of the 18 subscribers long videos brought in. It gets 10,135 impressions at 7.3% CTR and links to nothing.
- The old Foundayo video adds about 60 minutes a day from "foundayo" and "orforglipron" search.
- Food Noise, Strength and Side Effects earn mostly from suggested videos (RELATED_VIDEO).

The two engines that have ever produced volume are a fresh, searched drug name and suggested traffic. Neither is being fed.

**Production losses.**
- Of 10 long-video attempts from 11-17 to 11-22, 4 were lost and 1 of the 6 shipped was a duplicate.
- Foundayo What to Expect, the strongest current signal (old Foundayo video 536 min; Foundayo Short 834 views), has now failed 4 times: audio on 11-11, fact-check REVISE on 11-20 and 11-21, a broken render on 11-22.
- Serious Risks was held for beat drift: the render had 91% of cuts on time against 99% in the plan. Over two weeks, 6 holds share this one renderer fault.
- Months 2–6 was published a second time on 11-20 (8 views). That risks the repetitive-content policy and wasted a slot.

**No internal links.** Views from SHORTS and END_SCREEN are 0 on every long video (n≈37), and playlists have brought 2 views. The Studio links (Exp G) have waited 14 days. The best Shorts this week (Foundayo nausea 834, full the morning after 513, stomach pain 250) send viewers nowhere.

**Subscribers follow long-form views:** +8 this week. Long videos convert about 10× better per view than Shorts.
playbook_markdown:
# InforMed growth playbook (Growth Strategist, 2026-11-23)

**Status: off track.** 231 of 4,000 watch hours, +34 in 7 days (≈5 a day; the end of February needs ≈39). 394 subscribers, +8. New long videos win the click (3.7–6.6% CTR) but get only 64–124 impressions each. Minutes come from the back catalogue and drug-name search. **Priorities: ship Foundayo, chase searched drug names, never publish a duplicate, link everything.**

## Standing rules (owner, 2026-11-12; keep)
- Packaging keeps the gap. Titles and thumbnails never state the answer; state-change layouts are fine if the text keeps the question. The answer comes by 15 s (long) or 6 s (Shorts).
- Drug first. Shorts sentence 1 names tirzepatide (or the one drug the evidence is about) in ≤14 words, and scene 1's on-screen text matches it. Titles put the drug first.
- First frame is composed (character plus hook text at t=0). Shorts change shot at least every 2.5 s in the first 10 s. Never relax this.
- Long-form mix: Lane A is the base, plus 2–3 search-demand long videos a week: device how-to (Instructions for Use only, no amounts), what-to-expect timelines, label changes, approved-drug head-to-heads against tirzepatide. The "What is X?" ban covers unapproved pipeline drugs only.
- Shorts: at least 2 of 3 a day are a felt symptom or practical moment. A study supports a Short; it is never the topic.
- Shorts ending: one short safety line, then a line that loops into the first. Never a subscribe line or "link in the description" in a Short.

## Long-form (14:00 ET, 9–11 min; 2026-11-23)
- **No duplicates.** Before scripting and again before publishing, check the live channel list. Re-rendering a held video is fine. A second copy of a live title or topic never ships (Months 2–6 went out twice on 11-20).
- Title: drug first, the searched brand in brackets, then a question of ≤55 characters. Names people type: Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic, Foundayo, Wegovy pill.
- **Fast-turn takes the next slot:** a fresh randomized result naming a drug people search for gets a long video within 48 h, titled on the result (Exp I). (until 2026-12-14)
- Queue, one a day. If one is held, ship the next ready one; never leave the day empty:
  1. Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill: What to Expect. Last attempt, with every 11-22 fix: silent closing scene, remix to ≤0.02, counter-cropped heads, label escalation wording instead of "mostly", the full s21 list. If it's held again, park it and write a fresh 9-minute script from the label. (until 2026-11-30)
  2. Mounjaro vs Ozempic: Which Lowered A1C More? SURPASS-2 only: adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, 40 weeks, every arm vs semaglutide 1 mg as reported, no dose advice. (until 2026-11-30)
  3. Serious Risks: How Rare? Re-time it and apply the 11-21 fixes. (until 2026-11-30)
  4. Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) After 6 Months: What to Expect? Series part 3, using the label and SURMOUNT-1 to 72 weeks. Must not repeat Plateau or How Long. (until 2026-11-30)
  5. Zepbound Vial vs Pen (Instructions for Use only, no amounts), and only if the real IFU URL loads. (until 2026-11-30)
  - Backups (re-time before shipping): Injection Site Reactions (11-09), Burping and Heartburn (11-10). (until 2026-11-30)
- No new single-symptom long videos. Narrow topics go into chapters or Shorts.
- Ship-blockers: every cut within 0.5 s of its beat on the render; masking ≤0.02 on the final file; transcript matches the script word for word; the description ends "…whether it's right for you." The fact-checker and the Editor-in-Chief always win.

## Script structure (long-form; Exp H) (until 2026-12-07)
- Sentence 1: the drug, the title's question and the answer, with the "you" moment folded in. Never open with "Short answer." or a list, and never use a standalone "Picture this" scene.
- A second concrete payoff (a number or the first step) at 15–30 s. Keep any open loop to one sentence.
- Give the result and the population in one sentence (no "meet the trial" scenes). Land a payoff before about 70 s and re-hook every 45–75 s. Land the last new fact before 80%. Lists have 3 items at most. Never end a chapter on a warning card.
- One subscribe ask, after the payoff. End with "There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description." Never say "on screen".

## Linking (copywriter and publisher)
- The copywriter leaves line 1 empty and names one watch-next target in the post notes. The publisher adds the verified link.
- Targets:
  - new broad videos and Sleep Apnea → Side Effects
  - Side Effects → Stopping; Stopping → Keeping Results
  - First Month → Months 2–6 (Aqv2dOU-SmM only); Months 2–6 → How Long
  - Mounjaro vs Ozempic → Zepbound vs Wegovy; old Foundayo (LWyUfli67CI) → new Foundayo once it's live
  - EloraTZP → Side Effects
- Never link the duplicate MQqAwUKAKSI.
- Don't touch Strength or What to Eat until the Exp E read. (until 2026-11-24)

## Shorts (08:00 / 13:00 / 20:00 ET)
- Follow the task's `short-length` arm and `hook-archetype`. Never more than 160 spoken words.
- Topics that win, in order of proof:
  1. a visible body or pen moment, "Is this normal?", with the relief fact in the same sentence
  2. an approved drug name plus a felt symptom (Foundayo nausea 834, stomach pain 250)
- **20:00: the holiday table:** full fast, the morning after (513), bloating, stuffing. Target long video: Thanksgiving. (until 2026-11-27)
- From 2026-11-28, the 20:00 slot goes back to body, pen or approved-drug felt-symptom Shorts.
- Avoid:
  - diet tips with no felt moment (tiny plate 9, ginger ale 22, leftovers 25)
  - news, label or approval items; observational studies; pipeline drugs
  - cost, Medicare, pharmacy, surgery and grocery topics
  - "3 Ways" lists and brand-first titles
- Every Short logs one target long video in its post notes (Exp G): pen or injection → Pen how-to; hair → Hair Loss; stomach → Side Effects; holiday → Thanksgiving; Foundayo → Foundayo (LWyUfli67CI). (until 2026-12-14)

## Carousels
- Make one only if the scheduler asks, and reuse verified Short text only.

## Analyst (2026-11-23)
- Readouts: Exp E on 11-24; Pen at day 14 on 11-25; short-length on 11-26, recording which posts have day-7 data; First Month at day 14 on 11-27; Exp H as the curves arrive. (until 2026-11-30)
- Impressions at day 7 and day 14 for every new long video. Flag any broad video still under 200 impressions at day 14.
- Report the traffic source on each watch-next target, so we know whether description links bring any views.

experiments.name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail (What to Eat, plus Strength as a second test)
experiments.hypothesis: Our two most-shown practical videos have a packaging problem, not a discovery problem. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer that keeps the question lifts CTR toward 3.8–4.7%.
experiments.change: Only the thumbnail changes, with no body imagery. What to Eat was swapped around 11-04 and Strength on 11-10. No other edits to either video until 11-24.
experiments.metric: CTR on impressions after the swap vs CTR just before it (What to Eat about 1.9%, Strength about 0.6%), with views per day not falling. Success: 3.0% or more on both.
experiments.min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days per video, whichever comes later (read on 11-24)
experiments.result: Read tomorrow (11-24). Lifetime CTR has risen to 3.24% (What to Eat) and 2.59% (Strength), from about 1.9% and 0.6% before the swaps. That points to a lift, but these figures include the weeks before the swap, so read the after-swap window only. If both pass 3.0% after the swap, keep the thumbnails and add the line-1 links. Lifetime minutes: What to Eat 1,054, Strength 735 (+31 since 11-21).

experiments.name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double how often Shorts viewers subscribe.
experiments.change: The 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts ended with a subscribe line; the 20:00 Shorts were the control (11-03 to 11-17).
experiments.metric: Subscribers per 1,000 views at day 7, line vs control; channel subscribers per day vs the 1.3-a-day baseline.
experiments.result: Lost. Subscribers went from 382 to 386 in 14 days (about 0.3 a day against a 2.5 target), and every Short with data showed 0 subscribers. The line came out on 11-17. With the line gone, subscribers rose 8 in the last 7 days, almost all from long-form.

experiments.name: Exp G: Studio related-video link on top Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: The related-video link is the only clickable path from a Short. Setting it on our best body, pen and drug Shorts, aimed at the matching long video, will create Shorts traffic to long videos that converts to subscribers.
experiments.change:
The owner sets one related-video link per Short:
- hair grow-back and hair in women → Hair Loss
- injection site, injection sites, pen blood, bruise, pen dropped → Pen how-to
- nausea and stomach pain → Side Effects
- full the morning after → Thanksgiving
- Foundayo nausea → Foundayo (LWyUfli67CI)
No other change to these Shorts.
experiments.metric: Views and minutes from SHORTS on each target long video in the 7 days after the links are set, vs 0 before. Success: at least 1 long-video view per 100 new Short views across the set.
experiments.min_sample: 8 linked Shorts, 7 days after the links are set
experiments.result: Still not started after 14 days. The owner needs the channel's Google account signed in to Chrome. Views from SHORTS are still 0 on all ≈37 long videos. The targets now include Foundayo nausea (834 views) and full the morning after (513). The test starts the day the links are set.

experiments.name: Exp H: Second payoff at 15–30 s in long-form scripts
experiments.hypothesis: The biggest drop comes at 12–35 s, right after the first answer. A second concrete payoff (a number or the first step) at 15–30 s, with an open loop of one sentence at most, lifts the 30-second hold and the midpoint hold.
experiments.change: Every long video from 11-11 on uses this structure. Since 11-22 it also follows the analyst's rules: no "Short answer." label and no standalone "Picture this" scene.
experiments.metric: Day-7 median hold at 30 s and median relative hold at the midpoint, vs the baseline (30-second hold about 77%, midpoint about 44). Success: 30-second hold of 82% or more and a midpoint of 48 or more.
experiments.min_sample: 6 long videos built this way, at day 7
experiments.result: n=2 of 6. Alcohol held 94.5% at 30 s; First Month held 66.7%, losing 23 points at 14 s on a "Short answer." opener. Curves for How It Works, Keeping Results, Months 2–6, Nausea Foods and Mounjaro vs Zepbound are due over the next few days, so the readout should be possible by about 11-28. Too early to judge.

experiments.name: Exp I: Fast-turn long video on a fresh, searched drug name
experiments.hypothesis: New long videos stall at about 100 impressions because nothing new is being searched. A long video published within 48 h of a fresh randomized result naming a drug people search for gets at least 3× the impressions and minutes of a same-age Lane A video (the EloraTZP and Foundayo pattern).
experiments.change: When the radar finds a fresh randomized result for a searched drug name, it takes the next long slot within 48 h, titled on the result with the drug first (no "What is X?" for unapproved drugs). Nothing else in the format changes.
experiments.metric: Impressions, YT_SEARCH views and minutes at day 7 and day 14, vs the median of Lane A videos from 11-13 to 11-22 at the same age (about 100–140 impressions and about 40 minutes at days 4–8).
experiments.min_sample: 4 fast-turn long videos, or until 2026-12-14 (inconclusive if fewer than 4 qualifying results appear)
experiments.result: Starts 2026-11-23. Earlier anecdotes and signals: EloraTZP 5,255 minutes and 10,135 impressions; Foundayo 536; Petrelintide 320 on 472 impressions at 6.6% CTR; Survodutide 198; CagriSema 117.

experiments.name: short-length (owner): tight vs standard Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: Tighter Shorts (90–120 words, 40–55 s) earn more views and a higher average view percentage than standard ones (135–160 words, 65–80 s).
experiments.change: Each Short's task sets `tight` or `standard`, alternating by slot and day, from 11-12 to 11-26.
experiments.metric: Median views and average view percentage per arm at day 7.
experiments.min_sample: All Shorts from 11-12 to 11-26, each at day 7
experiments.result: Readout on 11-26; no winner yet. So far at day 7: standard median 44 views (n=7) vs tight 41.5 (n=6). Average view percentage 52.1% vs 42.6%. 15-second hold 68.8% (n=5) vs 70.6% (n=3). On 11-26 only Shorts posted up to about 11-19 will have day-7 data. Report the result with its n, and confirm on 12-03 if the arms are within 10%.

experiments.name: hook-archetype (owner): opening style for Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: Some of the 5 opening styles (result-first, negation, number-first, myth-flip, recognition-question) beat the others on views and average view percentage.
experiments.metric: Median views and average view percentage per style at day 7.
experiments.result: Don't read yet. Each style has n=5–7, and only 1–3 per style have day-7 views. Day-7 medians: myth-flip 112.5 (n=2), recognition 44 (n=3), result-first 42 (n=3), number-first 35 (n=3), negation 34.5 (n=2). Topic confounds every one of them.

experiments.name: Search-demand long videos vs Lane A (owner)
experiments.hypothesis: Device how-to, what-to-expect, label-change and approved-drug head-to-head long videos bring more search views and minutes than Lane A videos of the same age.
experiments.change: 2–3 of the week's long videos are search-demand videos. So far: Pen (11-11), First Month (11-13), Mounjaro vs Zepbound (11-18), Zepbound vs Wegovy (11-21), Sleep Apnea (11-22). Next: Foundayo, Mounjaro vs Ozempic, Vial vs Pen.
experiments.metric: Minutes and search views at day 14, matched by age.
experiments.result: Too early. First readouts: Pen on 11-25, First Month on 11-27. Anecdotes: Pen has 33 minutes and 14 of its 25 views came from search. First Month has 62 minutes at 7.3% CTR but only 124 impressions.

owner_decisions: Unlist the duplicate "Months 2–6" (MQqAwUKAKSI, 11-20, 8 views) today, and let the publisher refuse to publish any title that's already live. Why: two near-identical videos is exactly what YouTube's repetitive-content policy targets, right before a YPP review. The copy also splits the series' impressions (the original Aqv2dOU-SmM has 5.65% CTR). Expected effect: removes a monetization risk and stops wasted slots. This is the second production slip of this kind.

Spend 15 minutes in YouTube Studio once the channel's Google account is signed in to Chrome. These are the only steps the API can't do. (1) EloraTZP end screen → Side Effects and First Month. (2) Shorts related-video links: Foundayo nausea (834) → Foundayo LWyUfli67CI; full the morning after (513) → Thanksgiving, before 11-26; stomach pain (250) and nausea → Side Effects; hair → Hair Loss; injection, pen blood, bruise and pen dropped → Pen how-to. (3) End screens: Side Effects → Stopping, Stopping → Keeping Results, First Month → Months 2–6. Why: EloraTZP has about 40% of all long-form minutes and 10,135 impressions but sends viewers nowhere, and SHORTS/END_SCREEN views are 0 on all ≈37 long videos after 14 days of waiting. Expected effect: Exp G finally starts. Even 1 click per 100 Short views is about 15–30 long views a day, plus a second session on EloraTZP's daily traffic.

Let the publisher do the jobs the YouTube Data API supports, so they stop waiting on you: retitles, playlists and description links (videos.update, playlists.insert). Retitle Hair Loss (0.82% CTR) to "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Hair Loss: Why More in Women?", Constipation (1.43% on 629 impressions), Plateau (1.51% on 860) and Bones (2.16% on 786) to the analyst's titles. Create the playlist "Your First Months on Tirzepatide" (First Month, Aqv2dOU-SmM, How Long). Add line-1 watch-next links to the catalogue. Why: these have been pending for 2–3 weeks and none needs Studio. Expected effect: if Plateau and Bones simply reached the 4% channel median, together they'd gain roughly 30 views on the impressions they've already had, plus every future one. The series playlist gives the new 5.6–7.3% CTR videos a path from each other.

Have the renderer's cut timing and the final-file masking check fixed. Long videos: 6 holds in two weeks for beat drift (plans 96–100% on time, renders 76–91%). 7 holds for audio, including Foundayo on 11-22. 4 pieces shipped above the 0.02 masking limit. Why: over 11-17 to 11-22, 4 of 10 long-video attempts were lost, including the highest-signal video (Foundayo, attempted 4 times). Expected effect: about 2 more shipped long videos a week, and no more over-limit mixes reaching viewers.
